title: Chromatin Studio — build, inspect, and test a model
subtitle: An editable walkthrough of the actual application

delivery.timing_rule: Scene, keyframe and caption times are editable reference timings. The renderer scales each scene to its measured natural-paced neural narration plus a 1.25-second reading pause, rounded up to a video frame. Audio is never accelerated or truncated. Final timings are saved in render-timeline.json and render-manifest.json.
delivery.rendering_rule: Use actual application captures. A keyframe change represents the documented UI action. Pans and emphasis may help readability, but must not imply that a still image is a live trajectory. Do not fabricate events, data, bindings, RNA molecules, or successful cluster execution.
delivery.narration_engine: Local Kokoro-82M v1.0; af_heart voice; target 155 words per minute

Use real simulation steps to obtain any demonstrated bonds, contacts, polymerases or RNA. Retain the seed and run provenance used for those captures.

Pause before inspecting a state so the selected object and displayed measurements remain consistent.
Read the current UI before each capture. Actions below describe semantic targets rather than brittle screen coordinates.
display_notes: Choose a readable capture window before recording and use it consistently.
Capture full views and, where useful, a second close view of the actual panel. Do not crop away an uncertainty label or the distinction between draft and applied model.
Focus rectangles are intentionally unspecified. Set them from the captured layout after checking that the relevant text remains readable.

scenes.title: Start with the workbench
scenes.narration: Chromatin Studio connects a model builder, a spatial simulation, and measurements from the current run. Each chromatin bead is a stretch of DNA, and its size is a model setting. This walkthrough uses one size throughout: two hundred base pairs per bead, about one nucleosome and its linker. The example is Manuscript hypotheses at eighty kilobases: four hundred beads of two hundred base pairs each. The default model and the small presets all use this size. Only the twenty-megabase presets keep coarse ten-kilobase beads, each standing for many nucleosomes, and they are not shown here. The center shows the applied model. Builder changes belong to the draft until they are applied. Begin by checking the bead size, the run status, and the physical-clock label.

captions.text: Build on the left. Inspect the applied model in the center. Follow measurements and events.
Bead size is a setting. This tutorial uses 200 bp per bead throughout: about one nucleosome and its linker. 400 beads = 80 kb.
Draft settings and the current run are different. Check the scale and calibration status first.

scenes.title: Choose a focused experiment
scenes.narration: The Manuscript hypotheses example is the main model for this walkthrough. Each of its four hundred beads is two hundred base pairs, a coarse nucleosome unit that can be occupied or vacant. Nucleosome occupancy and individual transcripts are enabled. The preset includes transcription factors, coactivators, and illustrative active and repressive marks. These are starting hypotheses, not fitted biology. Expand builder gives the settings room. Ordinary edits stay in the draft until Apply and restart. How it works is a separate learning sandbox: its sliders explain equations without changing your run.

captions.text: “Manuscript hypotheses · 80 kb” is the main example, with nucleosome occupancy and individual RNA.
1 bead = 200 bp = one coarse nucleosome unit (occupied or vacant); 400 beads = 80 kb. No wrapped-DNA or histone-tail geometry.
“How it works” is a separate learning sandbox. Its controls leave the simulation unchanged.

scenes.title: Save your work, pick an engine, and grow a model
scenes.narration: Three everyday tools sit in the top bar. Import loads a model file into the draft, and Export saves the draft as a model file, so an experiment can be shared or rebuilt exactly. Save run downloads the applied model together with its current state and the history the server recorded. That is one snapshot plus measurements, not a full trajectory. Beside the Experiment menu, Engine chooses how the run is integrated. Brownian reference is the built-in engine used throughout this tutorial. Polychrom with OpenMM is an integration adapter: forces and reactions still run on the CPU. The Model tab lists which engines are installed here. Model size is no longer capped. In this example the chain was raised to five thousand beads, one megabase. The model still runs, but the notes below the observables now include a Large model warning, because the live engine and the 3D view were sized for about four thousand beads and six thousand particles. Open these model notes whenever you change a model.

captions.text: Import and Export move the draft model as a JSON file. Save run adds the current state and recorded history: one snapshot, not a trajectory.
Engine: Brownian reference (used here) or Polychrom/OpenMM, which still computes forces and reactions on the CPU.
No hard size cap. Above about 4,000 beads or 6,000 particles the model still runs, with a Large model note.

actions: Show the top bar: Import, Export and Save run, and the Experiment and Engine menus, with the 80 kb manuscript example applied.
Open the Model tab with Expand builder and show the engine cards, their local availability and the engine limitations.
In Chromatin, set Chromatin beads to 5,000, then Apply and restart.
Open the model notes and show the Large model warning beside the 5,112 / 6,000 particle counter.

accuracy_notes: Save run exports the applied configuration, the current state and the server-recorded history; it is not a trajectory and cannot supply an MSD.
The Polychrom/OpenMM adapter integrates on OpenMM but computes forces and reactions on the CPU. The native GPU engine is not selectable from the Engine menu.
Size limits are advisory since 2026-11-25: validation warns above the old sizes instead of rejecting the model. The 5,000-bead capture came from an isolated recording instance.

scenes.title: Set the confining domain
scenes.narration: The polymer already has confinement. System now makes the wall explicit: outside the chosen radius, a harmonic force pushes particles inward. Increasing wall stiffness reduces penetration; zero switches the force off. This is a soft wall, so particles are not clipped back to the boundary. The diagnostics report excursions for mechanical particles and released RNA. For a small locus, this sphere is a modeled domain, not automatically an entire nucleus. Compare radius and wall strength, because packing can change contacts and transcription even when every biochemical parameter stays the same.

captions.text: The soft wall pushes inward outside R: U = ½k max(r − R, 0)².
Wall strength 0 disables confinement. Small penetrations are allowed and reported.
The modeled domain is not automatically the whole nucleus. Control packing and wall effects.

actions: Open System and show radius and wall strength.
Expand builder and show the soft-wall illustration and actual excursion diagnostics.

accuracy_notes: Actual UI captures; all response parameters are illustrative unless independently calibrated.

scenes.title: Watch binding along the chromosome
scenes.narration: For a clearer view of binding, switch to a smaller example. In the Experiment menu it is called Live nucleosome access, twenty-five point six kilobases. That simply means a twenty-five point six kilobase stretch of chromatin: one hundred twenty-eight beads, still two hundred base pairs each, set up so that nucleosomes visibly control which sites proteins can reach. Open the one-dimensional genome and choose Live binding. Genes, nucleosome occupancy and directly bound proteins share one genomic axis. Navigate to a gene, then use Binding detail to see individual sites. Each molecule marker comes from a real chromatin bond; proximity alone is not binding. Run to watch bindings change, then pause and select a site. The table gives two rates for each protein. The association hazard is how often a nearby molecule binds, per unit of time. The release hazard is how often a bound molecule lets go; one over the release hazard is the average time it stays bound. Times remain reduced until an empirical physical mapping is attached. All tracks restores the wider view of marks, loops, polymerases and protein preferences.

captions.text: “Live nucleosome access · 25.6 kb”: a 25.6 kb region, 128 beads × 200 bp, built to show how nucleosomes control binding.
Live binding, then Binding detail, shows individual sites. Each marker is a real bond; proximity alone is not binding.
Association hazard: how often a nearby molecule binds. Release hazard: how often a bound one lets go; 1/release = mean time bound.

Protein glyphs represent actual direct molecule–chromatin attachments; multiple IDR domains do not become multiple molecules.
Capture hazards are not equilibrium Kd or macroscopic molar kon. Site release hazards use the current occupancy state.
This video uses paused captures from genuine engine runs; the app itself updates the view while running.

scenes.title: Create gaps and recruit remodelers
scenes.narration: Stay in the twenty-five point six kilobase nucleosome-access example. In Chromatin, define an initially vacant interval to create a nucleosome-free region. This sets the starting state; reassembly can fill the gap later. In Proteins, each species has separate multipliers for occupied and vacant sites: one scales how often it binds, the other how quickly it lets go. Opening a site can favor one species and disfavor another, especially when eviction also removes a mark. Add chromatin remodeler creates an editable species and enables occupancy in the draft. Its eviction, reassembly and sliding rates act when it is attached to chromatin or recruited through a configured transcription factor. Eviction clears marks. Reassembly starts unmarked. Sliding moves occupancy and its marks into an adjacent vacant bead, conserving nucleosome number. Inspect Recorded binding and remodeling events to follow what actually occurred. These are recent recorded events, not a complete microscopic history. Apply changes only when ready to start a new run.

captions.text: An initially vacant interval creates a starting gap. Reassembly and remodeling can change it later.
Set occupied/vacant capture and release independently for each species. A gap need not favor every protein.
Eviction clears marks; reassembly starts unmarked; sliding moves occupancy and marks to an adjacent vacant bead.
Inspect actual recorded events. Sliding conserves nucleosome number; the recent event buffer is not a full trajectory.

accuracy_notes: The 25.6 kb example is illustrative and uncalibrated; all rates and event times are reduced units unless a valid physical mapping is attached.
Sliding is an adjacent-bead relocation of binary occupancy and marks, not base-pair-resolved remodeling or DNA unwrapping.
Remodelers use prescribed kinetic rates; there is no ATP, explicit histone reservoir, remodeler mechanochemical cycle or persistent histone identity.
Occupancy-sensitive release changes chromatin bond hazards at reaction updates. It does not force immediate release on eviction or change protein–protein off-rates.

Binding and release records come from actual engine transitions. Turnover records report interval endpoint changes and mark-reset intervals; they do not enumerate every hidden turnover within an interval.
The recent event buffer is bounded; absence from the retained list is not evidence that a transition never occurred.
Initial occupancy intervals and editor changes remain draft settings until Apply and restart.
Binding/release/sliding carry sampled conditional times; turnover records carry interval endpoints. Event IDs order emitted observations, not a globally interleaved exact reaction timeline.

scenes.title: Add the whole nucleus and tethering elements
scenes.narration: Return to the eighty-kilobase example, open Bodies and add Whole nucleus. The modeled region still sits inside its own confinement sphere, while a much larger soft envelope represents the nuclear periphery. The region is a small part of the nucleus, so one side of it meets the envelope. By default that is the side away from the nucleolus, which faces the nuclear interior; you can move the envelope. Then add tethering elements: genomic intervals, such as lamina-associated domains, whose beads can attach to the envelope or to a landmark surface. Each bead within the capture distance attaches with its own hazard and, once attached, feels a spring to a fixed anchor. Attachment can require a mark and an occupied nucleosome, and vacant sites can release faster. In 3D, tick Whole nucleus to frame the envelope, and look for amber tether links. In 1D genome, the Tethers row shows attached beads, and the Nucleosomes row marks every vacant site. Tethers are phenomenological anchors, not lamina proteins.

captions.text: Bodies → Whole nucleus adds a soft envelope. The region meets it on the side away from the nucleolus, which faces the nuclear interior.
Tethering elements are genomic intervals. Beads within the capture distance attach stochastically and feel a spring to a fixed anchor.
Attachment can require a mark and an occupied nucleosome; vacant sites can release faster.
1D genome shows attached beads per element and every vacant nucleosome site. Tethers are phenomenological anchors.

actions: Use the isolated UI-check instance: the 80 kb model with a default-placed whole nucleus and one LAD tether over the H3K9me3 domain.
In 3D nucleus, tick Whole nucleus to frame the envelope around the territory.
Open Bodies → Whole nucleus & tethering in the expanded builder.
Show envelope stiffness, semi-axes, centre and the first tether element's interval and kinetics.
Untick Whole nucleus and zoom in to show amber tether links from attached beads to envelope anchors.

accuracy_notes: The capture model (recording-nucleus-tethers-model.json) uses an accelerated attach rate and a wider capture distance so attachments appear within a short UI run. It is a UI check, not a scientific model.
The envelope is a soft imposed wall; there is no lamina meshwork, pore complex, membrane mechanics or anchor diffusion.
Tether hazards are model inputs, not measured lamina-binding kinetics.
The OpenMM backends refuse models with a nuclear envelope or tethers; only the NumPy Brownian reference integrates them.

The envelope position follows the app's default, which places the peripheral side away from the nucleolus. Nuclear bodies are imposed fields inside the modeled region; nothing requires the nucleolus to sit at the periphery.

scenes.title: Define many proteins and their roles
scenes.narration: The rest of the walkthrough stays in the eighty-kilobase example. The Proteins editor defines each species independently. Expand builder gives these settings room. Set abundance, free diffusion, binding valence, mark preferences, and occupied-versus-vacant capture and release factors. A species can also write or erase a mark, or remodel nucleosomes. An IDR representation expands a molecule into a flexible chain of domain beads with binding stickers. This supports higher-order assemblies, but it is not an amino-acid-resolved protein model. Choose roles and interactions as explicit hypotheses; a biological name is not a calibrated parameter set.

captions.text: Use “Expand builder” to inspect each species’ abundance, free mobility, valence and chromatin preferences.
Writer, eraser and remodeling settings connect protein binding to chromatin-state changes.
IDRs are coarse domain-and-sticker chains. Biological names do not imply fitted molecular parameters.

accuracy_notes: Free molecular diffusion is an input; apparent bound or assembly mobility is an emergent measurement.

scenes.title: Inspect binding in its context
scenes.narration: The interaction view shows the current molecular network. Distinguish molecules with their own chromatin bond from those tethered indirectly through another protein. Protein pairs can bind while both are free, while one is directly chromatin-bound, or while both are bound. These are bond-mode links, the default. A pair can instead use attraction mode, which forms no bonds; the phase separation chapter covers it. The affinity calculator explores an ideal diffusion-limited association estimate after physical scales are supplied. Its nominal dissociation rate follows the requested Kd under independent, well-mixed assumptions. It does not turn the simulator's local encounter hazard into a measured molar association rate.

captions.text: Inspect free, directly bound and indirectly tethered molecules in the current binding network.
Assemblies can contain free–free, bound–free and bound–bound links. These are bond-mode links; attraction mode forms none.
The Kd calculator is an ideal physical estimate. It does not calibrate multivalent avidity or microscopic hazards.

accuracy_notes: The local on_rate is a per-eligible-pair inverse-time hazard, not M⁻¹ s⁻¹.

scenes.title: Connect accessibility, marks and stiffness
scenes.narration: Nucleosome occupancy is an explicit local state when this option is enabled. Eviction can expose a TF site, clears marks at that site, and changes the configured local persistence multiplier. Bound writers and recruited coactivators can alter marks; spreading follows three-dimensional chromatin contacts. Mark-dependent chromatin attraction is a separate interaction from a protein's mark preference. The learning example lets you compare occupied and vacant capture hazards and persistence values. Those numerical relationships explain a hypothesis; the illustration is not an equilibrium polymer calculation.

captions.text: Nucleosome eviction can alter TF access and local stiffness, while clearing local histone marks.
Protein mark preferences and chromatin–chromatin attraction are separate model mechanisms.
Compare occupied and vacant states in the guide, then inspect the corresponding applied-model tracks.

accuracy_notes: At coarse 10 kb resolution this is an effective bin state; the recording preset instead uses coarse 200 bp nucleosome units.
Persistence changes are configurable hypotheses, not universal consequences with a fixed sign.

scenes.title: Follow an enhancer to its target gene
scenes.narration: Regulation now shows the causal pathway for each gene. A transcription factor binds its configured region, and a coactivator is recruited through an actual protein bond. Enhancer contact can add to the target promoter's activation and initiation rates. The rate breakdown separates the baseline, recruitment, local mark gate and optional body response. Nucleosome occupancy changes transcription factor access; recruited enzymes can alter marks and accessibility. Basal activation can remain possible without recruitment. Losing contact removes its gain, but does not instantly turn an active promoter off or erase its chromatin memory.

captions.text: Define an enhancer’s interval, TF, coactivator and target gene in the Regulation builder.
Follow the causal map: recruitment × environment × mark gate determine effective activation.
Transcription is stochastic. Losing contact removes a rate gain; it does not instantly switch an ON promoter OFF.

accuracy_notes: Required/repressive marks at the gene start gate activation, not initiation by an already ON promoter.
TF region preferences are prescribed affinity multipliers, not sequence-motif scanning.
TF recruitment is a multiplicative gain above a basal factor of one, not a strict requirement for all transcription.

scenes.title: Watch polymerases produce individual RNA
scenes.narration: Transcription is stochastic. The engine now follows promoter switches within each reaction interval, and draws initiations only during the time actually spent active. Each new polymerase moves for the time remaining after its birth. Inspect its identity, position and growing RNA length in Elongation. Nucleosomes can slow movement; configured pauses have stochastic waiting times. Completed transcripts become diffusing points that can be processed or degraded. Nascent RNA can remain after a promoter switches off, so a nascent-positive gene is not the same as an active promoter.

captions.text: Initiations use actual time spent ON. New polymerases elongate only after their birth.
Advance real simulation time, pause, then select a molecule to inspect its identity and progress.
Promoter ON, nascent-positive, released and processed RNA are distinct observables.

scenes.title: Separate loops, assemblies and nuclear bodies
scenes.narration: Cohesin, protein assemblies and nuclear bodies organize space through different rules. Cohesin changes contacts through moving loop anchors. Protein bonds form higher-order assemblies. Speckles and the nucleolus are currently imposed fields, not self-generated condensates. In Genes, optional body responses can promote or suppress activation and initiation. A multiplier of one is neutral; the effect fades with promoter distance. These prescribed responses do not bypass the mark gate. Keep them separate from mechanical body attraction and from the speckle's effect on released RNA processing.

captions.text: Cohesin moves tethered anchors along chromatin; protein assemblies emerge from finite-valence bonds.
Speckles and nucleolus are imposed affinity fields. Their size and position are prescribed.
Body responses, mechanical affinity and RNA processing are separate hypotheses; multiplier 1 is neutral.

Highlight directional barriers and extrusion parameters without claiming a particular causal outcome.
Open the Genes builder in expanded mode.

accuracy_notes: The nucleolus has no explicit rRNA biogenesis or multiphase organization.
A visual cluster or fixed field does not establish calibrated condensate physics.

scenes.title: Grow droplets from attraction alone
scenes.narration: Phase separation at eighty kilobases shows a second way proteins can interact. Choose it from the Experiment menu. Around the same four hundred bead chain it places six hundred scaffold proteins and one hundred fifty clients, each a single bead. Open Interactions. These pairs use attraction mode: instead of forming bonds, two nearby proteins feel a shallow energy well. Here, Link strength is the well depth at contact, one and a half kT between scaffolds and nine tenths between client and scaffold, and Encounter radius is where the well ends. The association and dissociation rates are not used in this mode. This model needs hundreds of thousands of steps, more than the live engine reaches in a session, so the next states were advanced with the native engine and then opened in the workbench for display. At the preset's six hundred scaffolds, clusters of up to about forty molecules formed and dissolved again over four hundred thousand steps. Next, raise the scaffold count to one thousand and apply. Now dense droplets of about two hundred fifty molecules appear within about fifty thousand steps and persist, while about a fifth of their members are replaced every twenty-five thousand steps. Several droplets formed and had not merged by three hundred thousand steps. That contrast is what to look for: a dense phase that coexists with a dilute one, appears only above a threshold concentration, and keeps exchanging molecules. These are single runs, and an earlier GPU check did form one droplet at six hundred scaffolds, so the preset sits close to the threshold. Largest assembly stays at one, because it counts bonds. The well depth is not a measured affinity.

captions.text: Phase separation · 80 kb: 400 × 200 bp chain, 600 one-bead scaffolds and 150 clients.
Attraction mode: Link strength = well depth at contact (1.5 kT scaffold–scaffold, 0.9 kT client–scaffold); Encounter radius = where the well ends. Rates are unused.
Native-engine states opened in the workbench for display. At 600 scaffolds: clusters of up to ~40 form and dissolve.
Raise scaffolds to 1,000 and apply: droplets of ~250 molecules persist and keep exchanging members.
Phase separation = dense + dilute coexistence, a concentration threshold and exchange. Single runs; well depth is not a measured affinity.

scenes.title: Give the polymer a defensible physical clock
scenes.narration: Calibrate can import a condition-specific Hansen reference. Then supply a matched, equilibrated simulation and independent length evidence. Importing data does not complete calibration. Match the observable, dimension, drift treatment and fitting window. Next, load the synthetic example to practice fitting. Inspect its overlay, residuals and slopes; it cannot be applied as experimental evidence. A shared polymer clock converts reduced durations and rates consistently, but does not independently fit protein diffusion, binding residence times, elongation or Kd. Compatible empirical mappings retain their sources and baseline model fingerprint.

captions.text: Import a condition-specific Hansen reference. A matched equilibrated simulation and independent length evidence are still required.
Practice with the synthetic fit: inspect the overlay, residuals and slopes. Synthetic results remain demonstrations.
A shared clock converts units, not every biological parameter. Empirical mappings retain sources and a baseline-model fingerprint.

accuracy_notes: time_s is seconds per reduced time unit, not seconds per integration step.
A 2 s/reduced-time result in the synthetic example is generated teaching data, not a measured model clock.
A fitted source claim does not validate the entire model or establish a statistical confidence interval.
Importing a Hansen library reference provides measured input data but does not by itself establish a length scale or fitted clock.

scenes.title: Ask what the model actually reproduces
scenes.narration: The benchmark panel separates implementation checks, an ideal Rouse reference, and published-figure replication. Solid curves show sampled reference trajectories; dashed curves show analytical predictions. The saved suite tests free diffusion, internal-chain motion, center-of-mass diffusion and illustrative static-loop suppression. These fixtures exercise the actual Brownian integrator but bypass the production forces and coupled reaction system. Passing them is evidence about implementation. It is not a reproduction of every figure in the cited paper, and it supplies no experimental clock.

captions.text: Compare sampled reference trajectories with analytical curves, then inspect the saved checks and provenance.
Gaussian-chain reference fixtures test the Brownian integrator, not every production-model coupling.
Implementation agreement, empirical calibration and published-figure replication are separate achievements.

actions: Scroll to What have we reproduced? in Calibrate.
Show the actual saved pass count, reference curves and published-figure status.
Open Reference benchmark scope and limitations.
Show the saved observed/reference metrics and the explanation of what the fixture bypasses.

accuracy_notes: Refresh pass counts from the saved report when rebuilding the video; do not hard-code a historical count into narration.
Internal polymer curves remove center-of-mass translation; separate COM checks test whole-chain motion.
The current saved reference report does not claim full-paper replication.

scenes.title: Separate competition and shared environments
scenes.narration: Studies provides a simpler model for the manuscript's cis and trans comparison. Each simulated cell has four promoters: two genes on each of two homologs. All four share cell-wide variation. Genes on the same homolog may compete or experience a common fluctuating environment. The reference has no spatial polymer. Start with independent promoters, then add competition or shared environments separately. The experiment runs in isolation, leaving your current simulation untouched. Its purpose is to test whether a mechanism can produce a pattern, before asking whether the full spatial model or the experimental data support it.

scenes.title: Read correlations without confusing controls
scenes.narration: After the study finishes, compare cis and trans correlations and their difference. The interval reflects sampling uncertainty, not proof of causality. Switch between latent nascent activity, detected activity and promoter state; these observables answer different questions. The spatial pilot instead measures two genes on one chain across independent replicas. Its independent-replica null is not a trans-allele control. Download the plan and results to retain parameters, seeds and limitations. Reproducing the manuscript quantitatively still requires the underlying data, matched observation models, calibrated units and substantially longer converged experiments.

scenes.title: Check what the component tests actually showed
scenes.narration: Evidence shows the component tests that were actually run. Each study switches on one mechanism and compares the engine with its own rule, a closed-form result, or a published measurement. Those three levels are counted separately. The page only reads saved reports, so it runs nothing and leaves your simulation untouched. Select a study to see its figures. In the nucleosome kinetics study, based on Donovan and colleagues, blocking the site alone makes Reb1 and Cbf1 bind far too weakly. Matching their titrations requires slower release from the nucleosome. Hover for values, or open the table. Every check shows its accepted window, and experimental checks say whether they are input-matched, tuned, or a prediction. A pass under the provisional unit mapping is not a calibration. For a plain-language account of every mechanism and the check behind it, read the software paper in the docs folder.

captions.text: Numerical checks, closed-form references and published measurements are counted separately.

Each check shows its window and basis. A pass is not a calibration. The software paper (docs/paper) explains every check.

scenes.title: Export a reproducible cluster experiment
scenes.narration: When the model is ready, open Cluster job. Choose the device platform, independent replicas, output intervals and resource requests, then preview the scripts before exporting. The bundle carries the draft configuration, code, seeds and validation workflow for a fresh run. It does not resume the current live state. GPU use in an exported job is partial: forces, reactions and RNA run on the CPU, and only the integrator runs on the device, so speedup is not established. The faster native GPU engine, which runs bare polymers and the phase separation model, is used from Python and is not yet part of the exported job. Keep the model, inputs and results together, and use controlled comparisons to turn a visual hypothesis into testable evidence.

captions.text: Configure independent replicas, platform, sampling intervals and resources. Preview before exporting.
A bundle starts fresh from the draft. Exported jobs run only the integrator on the GPU; the native GPU engine is used from Python.
Build → inspect → calibrate → test. Preserve seeds, model provenance and controlled comparisons.
